## Create Functions

Create functions to support other analysis.

linear_regression_results_table: Function to run a series of linear models and return a summary table

get_summary_with_CI: Creating a summary table of the variable's Mean, SD, N, and CI

get_one_sample_results: Create a table with the t-test results of each variables against mu = 0

get_cont_descriptives: Summarize the continuous variables

```{r function}
#---------------------------------
# Function to run a series of linear models and return a summary table
#---------------------------------
# Inputs:
# 1. predictors: character vector of predictor variable names
# 2. outcome: character vector of outcome variable names (1 or more)
# Output: a summary table of the key parameters of the models
linear_regression_results_table <- function(predictors, outcomes, data = mot_clean) {
  # Fixed controls variables across models
  controls <- c("age", "gender", "income")
  
  # Loop over all outcome × predictor combinations
  results_list <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
    lapply(predictors, function(var) {
      # Build formula: outcome ~ predictor + controls
      formula_str <- paste(y, "~", paste(c(var, controls), collapse = " + "))
      f <- as.formula(formula_str)
      
      # Fit model
      fit <- lm(f, data = data)
      
      # Parameters
      s   <- summary(fit)
      coefs <- coef(s)
      est  <- coefs[var, "Estimate"]
      se   <- coefs[var, "Std. Error"]
      tval <- coefs[var, "t value"]
      pval <- coefs[var, "Pr(>|t|)"]
      
      # Effect size: semi-partial R^2 (ΔR^2)
      fit_reduced <- update(fit, paste(". ~ . -", var))
      semi_partial_r2 <- s$r.squared -
        summary(fit_reduced)$r.squared
      
      n <- nrow(model.frame(fit))
      
      # Create a df with descriptions and model parameters
      data.frame(
        outcome   = y,
        predictor = var,
        estimate  = est,
        std_error = se,
        t_value   = tval,
        p_value   = pval,
        semi_partial_r2  = semi_partial_r2,
        r_squared = s$r.squared,
        adj_r2    = s$adj.r.squared,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })
  })
  
  # Turn the outcomes × predictors parameters into one df
  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results_list, function(x)
    do.call(rbind, x)))
  
  # Round the other numeric columns to 2 digits
  num_cols <- c("estimate",
                "std_error",
                "t_value",
                "semi_partial_r2",
                "r_squared",
                "adj_r2")
  results[num_cols] <- lapply(results[num_cols], function(x)
    round(x, 2))
  
  # Return the results df
  return(results)
}

#---------------------------------
# Functions to create descriptive visualization dot plots
#---------------------------------
# ----- Prepare the data: get_summary_with_CI function -----
# Creating a summary table of the variable's Mean, SD, N, and CI
# Input: var_names (a list of names of the interested variables)
# Output: var_summary (a summary table of the variables' mean, sd, n, and CI)
get_summary_with_CI <- function(var_names) {
  # Reshape mot_clean to long format
  var_long <- mot_clean %>%
    # Select only the needed variables
    dplyr::select(all_of(var_names)) %>%
    # Transform into long format
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
                 names_to = "variable_name",
                 values_to = "rating")
  
  # Calculate Mean, SD, N, and CI
  var_summary <- Rmisc::summarySE(
    var_long,
    measurevar = "rating",
    groupvars = "variable_name",
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  
  # Reorder variable_name based on the mean rating
  var_summary <- var_summary %>%
    mutate(variable_name = fct_reorder(variable_name, rating))
  
  # Return the summary table
  return(var_summary)
}

# ----- t-test results table -----
# Create a table with the t-test results of each variables against mu = 0
# Input: A vector of variable names
# Output: t-test results table
get_one_sample_results <- function(var_names) {
  # For each variable name, create a row of results
  one_sample_results <- map_df(var_names, function(var_name) {
    data_vec <- mot_clean[[var_name]]
    data_vec <- data_vec[!is.na(data_vec)]
    # Run One-Sample T-test against 0
    t_res <- t.test(data_vec, mu = 0)
    # Calculate Cohen's d for one-sample
    d_res <- effectsize::cohens_d(data_vec, mu = 0)
    # Return results row
    data.frame(
      Variable = var_name,
      Mean     = round(mean(data_vec), 2),
      t_stat   = round(t_res$statistic, 2),
      df       = t_res$parameter,
      p_value  = t_res$p.value,
      Cohens_d = round(d_res$Cohens_d, 2),
      CI_Lower = round(d_res$CI_low, 2),
      CI_Upper = round(d_res$CI_high, 2)
    )
  })
  # Arrange by Effect Size
  one_sample_results <- one_sample_results %>%
    mutate(p_adj = round(p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni"), 3)) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs(Cohens_d)))
  
  return(one_sample_results)
}

#---------------------------------
# Create a function to summarize the continuous variables
#---------------------------------
# Input: A vector of variable names
# Output: Descrtiptive table
get_cont_descriptives <- function(num_vars) {
  # Create the summary table
  cont_descriptive <- t(sapply(num_vars, function(var_names) {
    x <- mot_clean[[var_names]]
    c(
      min       = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      max       = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean      = round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 2),
      sd        = round(sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 2),
      skewness  = round(skewness(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 2),
      kurtosis  = round(kurtosis(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 2)
    )
  }))
  
  # Reorder columns
  cont_descriptive <- as.data.frame(cont_descriptive)
  cont_descriptive$variable <- rownames(cont_descriptive)
  rownames(cont_descriptive) <- NULL
  cont_descriptive <- cont_descriptive[, c("variable", "mean", "sd", "min", "max", "skewness", "kurtosis")]
  
  # Round numeric columns
  cont_descriptive[, c("mean", "sd", "min", "max", "skewness", "kurtosis")] <-
    lapply(cont_descriptive[, c("mean", "sd", "min", "max", "skewness", "kurtosis")], function(x)
      round(as.numeric(x), 3))
  
  # Return the descrtiptive table
  return(cont_descriptive)
}

```

# Bivariate analysis
## Key variables

Descriptive and correlation table of key variables (prosociality/honesty-humility, TriPM, SDT, change goals, personality domains, age).

Correlation between prosocial-related variables (prosociality/honesty-humility and SDT parameters) -> confirm the link by examining the relationship between the honesty-humility trait and social discounting parameters.

```{r corr table key vars}
#---------------------------------
# Bivariate analysis - key vars
#---------------------------------
# Variables of interest
var_cols <- c(
  "change_goal_initial",
  "change_goal_final",
  "prosociality",
  "TriPM_total",
  "AUC",
  "k_exponential",
  "age"
)

# ----- Creating correlation table -----
apa.cor.table(mot_clean[, var_cols], table.number = 2, filename = "../Figures/Correlations.doc")

# ----- Calculate correlation between vars of interest -----
# Correlation between Honesty-humility and AUC
cor.test(mot_clean$prosociality, mot_clean$AUC, method = "pearson")

# Correlation between Honesty-humility and k_exponential
cor.test(mot_clean$prosociality, mot_clean$k_exponential, method = "pearson")

# Correlation between Honesty-humility and TriPM_total
cor.test(mot_clean$prosociality, mot_clean$TriPM_total, method = "pearson")

# Correlation between Honesty-humility and TriPM_meanness
cor.test(mot_clean$prosociality, mot_clean$TriPM_meanness, method = "pearson")

# Correlation between Honesty-humility and TriPM_boldness
cor.test(mot_clean$prosociality, mot_clean$TriPM_boldness, method = "pearson")

# Correlation between Honesty-humility and TriPM_disinhibition
cor.test(mot_clean$prosociality,
         mot_clean$TriPM_disinhibition,
```

# Goal One: Prosociality change goals

## Initial prosociality change goal

The following block calculated the percentage of participants who wanted to be more, less prosocial, or stay the same. It also tests the extent to which individuals’ prosociality level is linked to their prosociality change goals.


```{r characteristics and change goals}
#---------------------------------
# Participants initial change goals >0, <0, or =0
#---------------------------------
# ----- initial change goal -----
# % wanting to be less prosocial
sum(mot_clean$change_goal_initial < 0) / nrow(mot_clean)
# % wanting to be more prosocial
sum(mot_clean$change_goal_initial > 0) / nrow(mot_clean)
# % wanting to stay the same
sum(mot_clean$change_goal_initial == 0) / nrow(mot_clean)

#---------------------------------
# Initial change goal vs prosociality
#---------------------------------
# With control var only
control_model <- lm(change_goal_initial ~ age + gender + income, data = mot_clean)

# With prosocial predictor
prosocial_model <- lm(change_goal_initial ~ prosociality + age + gender + income, data = mot_clean)

# Check assumptions
plot(prosocial_model)

# Summarize prosocial model
summary(prosocial_model)

```

# Goal Two: Conditions' effects on change goals
Second, we examine whether psychoeducation or feedback on their own prosociality is effective in inspiring prosociality improvements among individuals with different characteristics.

```{r motivations changes vs prosociality prep}
#---------------------------------
# Data prep
#---------------------------------
# Select variables for analysis
MEM_var <- mot_clean %>%
  select(
    # id, condition order, & controls
    participant_id,
    feedback_first,
    age,
    gender,
    income,
    
    # prosociality & psychopathy
    prosociality,
    TriPM_total,
    
    # change goal variables
    change_goal_initial,
    change_goal_final,
    change_goal_pre_feedback,
    change_goal_post_feedback,
    change_goal_pre_psychoed,
    change_goal_post_psychoed
  )
```

## All conditions

Compare the change goals before and after all conditions (psychoed + feedback).

### Models

```{r motivations changes vs prosociality all conditions}
#---------------------------------
# Prep
#---------------------------------
# Transform MEM_var from long to wide
mot_all <- MEM_var %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(change_goal_initial, change_goal_final),
    names_to = "time_all_conditions",
    values_to = "change_goal_all_condition"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    time_all_conditions = dplyr::recode(
      time_all_conditions,
      change_goal_initial = "Initial",
      change_goal_final   = "Final"
    )
  )

# Factor time and reorder
mot_all$time_all_conditions <- factor(mot_all$time_all_conditions, levels = c("Initial", "Final"))

#---------------------------------
# Models
#---------------------------------
# ----- Standardize -----
mot_all_z <- mot_all

# z-score outcome + continuous predictors
mot_all_z$change_z        <- as.numeric(scale(mot_all_z$change_goal_all_condition))
mot_all_z$prosociality_z  <- as.numeric(scale(mot_all_z$prosociality))
mot_all_z$age_z           <- as.numeric(scale(mot_all_z$age))
mot_all_z$income_z        <- as.numeric(scale(mot_all_z$income))

# ----- Baseline models -----
model_empty_z <- lmer(change_z ~ 1 +
                        (1 | participant_id), data = mot_all_z)
summary(model_empty_z)

model_control_z <- lmer(change_z ~ age_z + gender + income_z +
                          (1 | participant_id), data = mot_all_z)
summary(model_control_z)

model_x_interaction_z <- lmer(
  change_z ~ time_all_conditions + prosociality_z +
    age_z + gender + income_z +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = mot_all_z
)
summary(model_x_interaction_z)

# ----- Interaction Model - standardized -----
# Time x prosocial model
model_all_z <- lmer(
  change_z ~ time_all_conditions * prosociality_z + age_z + gender + income_z + (1 |
                                                                                   participant_id),
  data = mot_all_z
)
summary(model_all_z)

tab_model(
  model_all_z,
  show.se = TRUE,
  show.stat = TRUE,
  show.ci = FALSE,
  p.style = "numeric",
  show.aic = FALSE,
  show.icc = FALSE,
  string.est = "Estimate",
  string.se = "SE",
  string.stat = "t",
  string.p = "p"
)

# Check assumptions
plot(model_all_z)
qqnorm(resid(model_all_z))
qqline(resid(model_all_z))

# ----- Interaction Model - non-standardized-----
# Time x prosocial model
model_all <- lmer(
  change_goal_all_condition ~ time_all_conditions * prosociality +
    age + gender + income +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = mot_all
)

summary(model_all)

```

### Graph

```{r motivations changes vs prosociality all conditions - graphs}
#---------------------------------
# Graph - line graph
#---------------------------------
# Estimated marginal means
emm <- emmeans(model_all,
               ~ time_all_conditions | prosociality,
               at = list(prosociality = c(
                 mean(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE) -
                   sd(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE),
                 mean(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE),
                 mean(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE) +
                   sd(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE)
               )))
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm)

# Factor prosociality levels and time points
emm_df$prosociality_f <- factor(emm_df$prosociality,
                                labels = c("Low (−1 SD)", "Mean", "High (+1 SD)"))
emm_df$time_all_conditions <- factor(emm_df$time_all_conditions, levels = c("Initial", "Final"))

# Create graph using the estimated marginal means
all_conditions_plot <- ggplot(
  emm_df,
  aes(
    x = time_all_conditions,
    y = emmean,
    group = prosociality_f,
    color = prosociality_f,
    shape = prosociality_f
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
                width = 0.07,
                linewidth = 1.0) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (All Conditions)",
    y = "Predicted Change Goal",
    color = "Prosociality",
    shape = "Prosociality"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 17.5)

# Print graph
all_conditions_plot
```

### Estimated marginal means

```{r motivations changes vs prosociality all conditions - Estimated marginal means}
# Define the low and high prosociality
pros_levels <- c(
  mean(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE) -
    sd(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE) +
    sd(mot_clean$prosociality, na.rm = TRUE)
)
pros_labels <- c("Low Prosociality", "Mean Prosociality", "High Prosociality")

# Estimated marginal means
emm <- emmeans(model_all,
               ~ time_all_conditions | prosociality,
               at = list(prosociality = pros_levels))
contrast(emm, method = "pairwise")
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm) %>%
  mutate(prosoc_group = factor(prosociality, levels = pros_levels, labels = pros_labels))

# Pairwise time contrast within each prosociality value
con_df <- contrast(emm, method = "pairwise") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(prosoc_group = factor(prosociality, levels = pros_levels, labels = pros_labels))

```

## Feedback condition

Compare the change goals before and after the feedback condition.

Only include the participants who completed the feedback condition first (n = 102).

### Models

```{r motivations changes vs prosociality feedback}
#---------------------------------
# Prep
#---------------------------------
# Transform MEM_var from long to wide
mot_feedback <- MEM_var %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(change_goal_pre_feedback, change_goal_post_feedback),
    names_to = "time_feedback",
    values_to = "change_goal_feedback"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    time_feedback = dplyr::recode(
      time_feedback,
      change_goal_pre_feedback  = "Pre-feedback",
      change_goal_post_feedback = "Post-feedback"
    )
  )

# Factor time and reorder
mot_feedback$time_feedback <- factor(
  mot_feedback$time_feedback,
  levels = c("Pre-feedback", "Post-feedback")
)
# Keep only when the participant completed the feedback condition first
mot_feedback <- mot_feedback %>%
  filter(feedback_first == 1)

#---------------------------------
# Models
#---------------------------------
# ----- Standardize -----
mot_feedback_z <- mot_feedback

# z-score outcome + continuous predictors
mot_feedback_z$change_z        <- as.numeric(scale(mot_feedback_z$change_goal_feedback))
mot_feedback_z$prosociality_z  <- as.numeric(scale(mot_feedback_z$prosociality))
mot_feedback_z$age_z           <- as.numeric(scale(mot_feedback_z$age))
mot_feedback_z$income_z        <- as.numeric(scale(mot_feedback_z$income))

# ----- Baseline models -----
model_empty_z <- lmer(change_z ~ 1 +
                        (1 | participant_id), data = mot_feedback_z)
summary(model_empty_z)

model_control_z <- lmer(change_z ~ age_z + gender + income_z +
                          (1 |
                             participant_id), data = mot_feedback_z)
summary(model_control_z)

model_x_interaction_z <- lmer(
  change_z ~ time_feedback + prosociality_z +
    age_z + gender + income_z +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = mot_feedback_z
)
summary(model_x_interaction_z)

model_time_z <- lmer(
  change_z ~ time_feedback +
    age_z + gender + income_z +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = mot_feedback_z
)
summary(model_time_z)

# ----- Interaction Model - standardized -----
# Time x prosocial model
model_feedback_z <- lmer(
  change_z ~ time_feedback * prosociality_z + age_z + gender + income_z + (1 |
                                                                             participant_id),
  data = mot_feedback_z
)

summary(model_feedback_z)

tab_model(
  model_feedback_z,
  show.se = TRUE,
  show.stat = TRUE,
  show.ci = FALSE,
  p.style = "numeric",
  show.aic = FALSE,
  show.icc = FALSE,
  string.est = "Estimate",
  string.se = "SE",
  string.stat = "t",
  string.p = "p"
)

# Check assumptions
plot(model_feedback_z)
qqnorm(resid(model_feedback_z))
qqline(resid(model_feedback_z))

# ----- Interaction Model - non-standardized-----
# Time x prosocial model
model_feedback <- lmer(
  change_goal_feedback ~ time_feedback * prosociality +
    age + gender + income +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = mot_feedback
)

summary(model_feedback)

```

## Psychoed condition

Compare the change goals before and after the psychoed condition.

Only include the participants who completed the psychoed condition first (n = 98).

### Models

```{r motivations changes vs prosociality, psychoed condition}
#---------------------------------
# Prep
#---------------------------------
# Transform MEM_var from long to wide
mot_psychoed <- MEM_var %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(change_goal_pre_psychoed, change_goal_post_psychoed),
    names_to = "time_psychoed",
    values_to = "change_goal_psychoed"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    time_psychoed = dplyr::recode(
      time_psychoed,
      change_goal_pre_psychoed  = "Pre-psychoed",
      change_goal_post_psychoed = "Post-psychoed"
    )
  )

# Factor time and reorder
mot_psychoed$time_psychoed <- factor(mot_psychoed$time_psychoed,
                                         levels = c("Pre-psychoed", "Post-psychoed"))
# Keep only when the participant completed the psychoed condition first
mot_psychoed <- mot_psychoed %>%
  filter(feedback_first == 0)

#---------------------------------
# Models
#---------------------------------
# ----- Standardize -----
mot_psychoed_z <- mot_psychoed

# z-score outcome + continuous predictors
mot_psychoed_z$change_z        <- as.numeric(scale(mot_psychoed_z$change_goal_psychoed))
mot_psychoed_z$prosociality_z  <- as.numeric(scale(mot_psychoed_z$prosociality))
mot_psychoed_z$age_z           <- as.numeric(scale(mot_psychoed_z$age))
mot_psychoed_z$income_z        <- as.numeric(scale(mot_psychoed_z$income))

# ----- Baseline models -----
model_empty_z <- lmer(change_z ~ 1 +
                        (1 |
                           participant_id), data = mot_psychoed_z)
summary(model_empty_z)

model_control_z <- lmer(change_z ~ age_z + gender + income_z +
                          (1 |
                             participant_id), data = mot_psychoed_z)
summary(model_control_z)

model_x_interaction_z <- lmer(
  change_z ~ time_psychoed + prosociality_z +
    age_z + gender + income_z +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = mot_psychoed_z
)
summary(model_x_interaction_z)

# ----- Interaction Model - standardized -----
# Time x prosocial model
model_psychoed_z <- lmer(
  change_z ~ time_psychoed * prosociality_z + age_z + gender + income_z + (1 |
                                                                               participant_id),
  data = mot_psychoed_z
)
summary(model_psychoed_z)

tab_model(
  model_psychoed_z,
  show.se = TRUE,
  show.stat = TRUE,
  show.ci = FALSE,
  p.style = "numeric",
  show.aic = FALSE,
  show.icc = FALSE,
  string.est = "Estimate",
  string.se = "SE",
  string.stat = "t",
  string.p = "p"
)

# Check assumptions
plot(model_psychoed_z)
qqnorm(resid(model_psychoed_z))
qqline(resid(model_psychoed_z))

# ----- Interaction Model - non-standardized-----
# Time x prosocial model
model_psychoed <- lmer(
  change_goal_psychoed ~ time_psychoed * prosociality +
    age + gender + income +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = mot_psychoed
)

summary(model_psychoed)

```

### Motivational effectiveness of psychoeducational information

The following block tests whether the information we provided in the psychoed condition motivated people, and whether participants with different prosociality levels found them differently motivating.

```{r motivators}
# List of the prosocial motivator variables
motivator <- c(
  "Mot_wellbeing",
  "Mot_stress",
  "Mot_religion",
  "Mot_moral",
  "Mot_emotion",
  "Mot_meaning",
  "Mot_health",
  "Mot_reputation",
  "Mot_connection",
  "Mot_better_friends",
  "Mot_job",
  "Mot_contagion",
  "Mot_romantic",
  "Mot_norm",
  "Pro_score_reaction"
)

#---------------------------------
# Linear regression
#---------------------------------
# Predictor of interest: prosociality
prosocial_predictors <- c("prosociality")

# Run the linear_regression_results_table function
# Predictor: prosociality
# Outcomes: prosocial motivator variables
model_table <- linear_regression_results_table(predictors = prosocial_predictors, outcome = motivator)

# Apply Bonferroni correction
model_table$adjusted_p_value <- p.adjust(model_table$p_value, method = "bonferroni")
model_table <- model_table %>%
  relocate(adjusted_p_value, .after = p_value) %>%
  mutate(across(c(p_value, adjusted_p_value), ~ round(.x, 5)))

# Print table
DT::datatable(model_table,
              caption = "The relationship between prosociality and the effectiveness of the motivational information, controlling for age, gender, and income",
              options = list(
                autoWidth = TRUE
              ))

#---------------------------------
# Create the summary tables
#---------------------------------
# Create table using the get_cont_descriptives function
motivator_descriptives <- get_cont_descriptives(motivator)
# Rank from highest mean to lowest
motivator_descriptives <- motivator_descriptives %>%
  arrange(desc(mean))
# Print the summary table
knitr::kable(motivator_descriptives, caption = "Descriptives of the Effectiveness of the Motivational Information")

# Create table using the get_one_sample_results function
motivator_t_test <- get_one_sample_results(motivator)
# Print the summary table
knitr::kable(motivator_t_test, caption = "One Sample T-Test Results of the Effectiveness of the Motivational Information")

#---------------------------------
# Create the dot graph with CI - Separated
#---------------------------------
# Creating a summary table of the effectiveness ratings' Mean, SD, N, and CI using the get_summary_with_CI function
motivator_summary_with_CI <- get_summary_with_CI(motivator)
# Drafting a dot plot of mean effectiveness ratings with CI
motivator_dot_plot <- ggplot(motivator_summary_with_CI, aes(x = variable_name, y = rating)) +
  # Draw the error bars
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = rating - ci, ymax = rating + ci),
                width = 0.2,
                color = "gray50") +
  # Draw the mean points
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#2c7fb8") +
  
  # Set range
  # Remane the lables
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  
  # Rename variables
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "Mot_wellbeing" = "Well-being",
      "Mot_stress" = "Stress",
      "Mot_religion" = "Faith",
      "Mot_moral" = "Morality",
      "Mot_emotion" = "Emotions",
      "Mot_meaning" = "Sense of Purpose",
      "Mot_health" = "Physical Health",
      "Mot_reputation" = "Reputation",
      "Mot_connection" = "Social Connectedness",
      "Mot_better_friends" = "Social Network",
      "Mot_job" = "Profession",
      "Mot_contagion" = "Ripple Effect",
      "Mot_romantic" = "Romantic Appeal",
      "Mot_norm" = "Social Norm",
      "Pro_score_reaction" = "Effect of Feedback"
    )
  ) +
  
  # Flip coordinates for easier reading
  coord_flip(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(y = "Self-Rated Motivational Effectiveness of Psychoeducational Information", caption = ".")

# Print plot
motivator_dot_plot

# Save plot
ggsave(
  filename = "../Figures/Figure 3_Mean Ratings of the Motivational Effectiveness of Psychoeducational Information.png",
  plot = motivator_dot_plot,
  width = 6,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300
)

```

## Graphs - Combine & Export

Combine the plots of the interactions between time and prosociality on the prosociality change goal in the feedback condition, psychoed condition, and all conditions. 

```{r combine graphs}
# Make the range same across plots
psychoed_condition_plot <- psychoed_condition_plot + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.25, 2))+ labs(title = "psychoed Condition")
feedback_condition_plot <- feedback_condition_plot + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.25, 2))+ labs(title = "Feedback Condition")+ theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())
all_conditions_plot <- all_conditions_plot + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.25, 2))+ labs(title = "All Conditions")+ theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())

psychoed_condition_plot
feedback_condition_plot
all_conditions_plot

# Combine plots side-by-side into one graph
combined_plot <- psychoed_condition_plot + feedback_condition_plot + all_conditions_plot +
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 3,
    guides = "collect",
    axis_titles = "collect",
    widths = c(1, 1, 1)
  ) +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = 
      "a")&
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.position = "right",
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )

# Print graph
combined_plot

# Save graph
ggsave(
  filename = "../Figures/Figure 2_The interactions between time and prosociality on the prosociality change goal.png",
  plot = combined_plot,
  width = 15,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)

```
